notes: El Molino / Rio Ojotska (Cooper), a two-grant exchange. (1) Rio Ojotska (aka Rio del Sacramento) granted by Figueroa, decreed Dec 23 1833 / título Dec 31 1833, Deputation-approved May 17 1834 (expediente 'A'/'B', transcript p16-29). Cooper found it inconvenient and EXCHANGED it with the government for (2) El Molino (Levanta hyeme) in Sonoma Co., granted by Nicolas Gutierrez in 1836. The register's rancho 'Molinos' + year 1836 track the El Molino grant, but its governor 'Jose Figueroa' belongs to the surrendered Ojotska tract, hence governor ERR = Gutierrez. Hoffman lists both ('1833 by Figueroa, and Feb 24 1836 by Nicolas Gutierrez'). The El Molino título itself ('C'/'D', Gutierrez) sits later in the transcript than the ~35 pages read but is verbatim recited in the petition (p4) and by Vallejo (p7). Claim confirmed by the Board Nov 14 1854.

notes: Morro y Cayucos (Case 155 SD, Comm. No. 529). Rancho = two adjacent one-league tracts: El Morro (to Martín Olivera) and Los Cayucos (to Vicente Feliz), BOTH definitively granted by Gov. name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE No. 53 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / RANCHO del PASO GRANT / SAMUEL NORRIS / CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 transcript title page 'Rancho del Paso'; grant title translation PDF p16 (CASE 53 ND PAGE 11) 'the location which forms past-land named Rancho del Paso situated on the North Bank of the American River'.

year.evidence: PDF p17 (CASE 53 ND PAGE 12), close of the title translation: 'Given in Monterey the 20th of December 1844. Manuel Jimeno Secy. Manuel Micheltorena.' District Court decree PDF p76 (PAGE 68): 'made by Gov. Micheltorena on the 20th day of Dec. 1844 to Eliab Grimes'.

governor.evidence: PDF p16 (PAGE 11), head of the title: 'Citizen Manuel Micheltorena Brigadier General of the Mexican Army ... Governor & the Commandant General and Inspector of the Department of Californias'; signed 'Manuel Micheltorena' PDF p17 (PAGE 12). Micheltorena's own marginal decree on the expediente, PDF p15 (PAGE 10): 'Monterey Dec. 1844 / Let the title be issued as asked. Micheltorena'.

grantee.evidence: PDF p16 (PAGE 11) title translation: 'Whereas Don Eliab Grimes a naturalized Mexican has asked for his personal benefit the location which forms past-land named Rancho del Paso ... I have in the name of the Mexican Nation ceded to him the before mentioned land declaring him to be the proprietor thereof by these present letters.' The expediente petition, PDF p14 (PAGE 9), is headed 'Presented by the naturalized citizen Eliab Grimes' and signed 'Monterey Dec. 16th 1844 Eliab Grimes'. Samuel Norris is the U.S.-era claimant only: the petition PDF p9 (PAGE 4) states the tract 'was granted by Michel Torrena Govr of Upper California by a concession dated the 21th of Dec 1844 to one Eliab Grimes a naturalized citizen of the Mexican Nation, which said Grimes dying bequeathed said tract of land by a Codicil added to his will dated 18th of April 1845 to one Hiram Grimes and by said Hiram sold and conveyed to this petitioner by deed dated the 8th day of August 1849.'

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE No. 53 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; every leaf stamped 'CASE 53 ND'; District Court wrapper PDF p49 'U.S. DISTRICT COURT, Northern District of California, No. 53'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_nd053.pdf. (Board docket was No. 146, PDF p5 and the p48 certificate, matching Hoffman's commission_no 146.)

outcome.evidence: PDF p47 (CASE 53 ND PAGE 34) Board decree: 'It is decreed that the said claim be confirmed to the extent of ten square leagues ... Given under our hands this 18th day of April 1853' (Hiland Hall, Harry J. Thornton), filed 22 April 1853. The US appealed (AG Cushing, 11 Sept 1854, PDF p50 and p52, PAGES 36 and 38; notice of appeal filed 21 Oct 1854, PDF p51). The appeal was decided for the claimant: US District Court, Northern District, opinion PDF p72-75 (PAGES 64-67) 'The decision of the Commissioners in favor of its validity must therefore be affirmed', and decree PDF p75-76 (PAGES 67-68) 'It is ordered, adjudged and decreed that the decision of said Board be affirmed. And it is hereby further ordered, adjudged and decreed that the claim of the appellee be confirmed to the extent of ten square leagues to the land described in the grant made by Gov. Micheltorena on the 20th day of Dec. 1844 to Eliab Grimes.' Norris's own sworn affidavit, PDF p70 (PAGE 61), adds that 'the appeal to the Supreme Court of the United States [was] dismissed by order of the Attorney General of the United States.'

corrections.grantee: Eliab Grimes per the grant itself, PDF p16 (CASE 53 ND PAGE 11): 'Whereas Don Eliab Grimes a naturalized Mexican has asked for his personal benefit the location ... named Rancho del Paso'. Samuel Norris took by mesne conveyance: Eliab Grimes (d. 1848) devised the rancho by codicil of 18 April 1845 to his nephew Hiram Grimes, who deeded it to Norris 8 August 1849 (PDF p9, PAGE 4; will and probate at PDF p18-20, PAGES 13-15).

notes: Dominant error class again: the register carries the U.S. claimant (Samuel Norris, the name on the red label) where the Mexican grantee belongs. Hoffman 1862 ('Eliab Grimes') agrees with the case file against the register. Year and governor in the register are correct. One internal discrepancy in the file, not affecting a grade: the claimant's petition (PDF p9) dates the concession '21th of Dec 1844' while the file's own sworn translation of the title (PDF p17) and the District Court decree (PDF p76) both give 20 December 1844. John A. Sutter's deposition (PDF p11-14, PAGES 5-8) is the key testimony: he gave Grimes a provisional right to settle in 1841 and, as sole civil judge of the Sacramento district, gave formal possession after the grant. Patent not in the file; Phase C should check GLO for the claimed 4 May 1858 patent no. 96 to Samuel Norris. Curator note at PDF p80 points to related papers at BANC MSS C-I 16, Pt. I:94.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE No. 351 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / PASO DE ROBLES GRANT / PETRONILLA RIOS / CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 transcript title page 'Paso de Robles'; expediente cover PDF p18 (351 SD PAGE 13) 'en solicitud del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles'.

year.evidence: PDF p21 (351 SD PAGE 16), Micheltorena's concession decree: 'Monterrey Mayo doce de 1844. Vista la peticion con que da principio este Espediente, los informes que preceden ... declaro dueno en propiedad a D.n Pedro Narvaez del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles ... en extension de seis sitios de ganado mayor.' Board opinion PDF p36: 'a grant issued in pursuance thereof by Governor Michelltorena, bearing date the 12th day of May, 1844'.

governor.evidence: PDF p21 (PAGE 16), closing formula of the decree: 'El Sor. D. Manuel Micheltorena Gobernador, Comandante General asi lo mando, decreto y firmo'; Micheltorena also signs the 16 May 1844 boundary-settlement act on the same leaf, with Manuel Jimeno as Secretario del Despacho. His earlier marginal orders on the expediente are at PDF p20 (PAGE 15), 'Monterey Nov.e 27 de 1843 ... Micheltorena'.

grantee.evidence: PDF p21 (PAGE 16), the decree itself: 'declaro dueno en propiedad a D.n Pedro Narvaez del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles'. The expediente is headed (PDF p18, PAGE 13) '1844 Espediente. Promovido por el Sor. Capitan D.n Pedro Narvaes en solicitud del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles. Numero 375', and the underlying petition (PDF p20, PAGE 15) is signed 'Monterrey Nov.e 26 de 1843. Pedro Narvaez', describing himself as '1er teniente de la armada nacional y capitan de este puerto'. Petronilo Rios is the U.S.-era claimant, a purchaser: the Board's own opinion (PDF p36) says 'The petitioner in this case asks a confirmation as grantee of Don Pedro Narvaez ... and also a deed from the said Narvaez to the present claimant dated the 30th day of March 1846.'

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE No. 351 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; leaves stamped '351 SD'; District Court wrapper PDF p42 'U.S. DISTRICT COURT, Southern District of California, No. 351 ... Transcript of the Record from the Board of U.S. Land Commissioners, In Case No. 241, Filed Dec. 6, 1855'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd351.pdf. (Board docket No. 241, matching Hoffman's commission_no 241.)

outcome.evidence: PDF p37 Decree of Confirmation, 'Petronillo Rios vs The United States, No. 241': 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the said Petitioner is valid and it is therefore decreed that his application for a confirmation thereof be allowed. The land of which confirmation is hereby given ... is known by the name of "Paso de Robles", containing six square leagues' (R. Aug. Thompson and S. B. Farwell, Commissioners), filed 3 July 1855. The US noticed an appeal (AG Cushing 31 Dec 1855, PDF p45, PAGE 33; notice of appeal filed 12 Feb 1856, PDF p46, PAGE 34) and US Attorney Pacificus Ord filed a petition on appeal 5 January 1857 (PDF p48-50, PAGES 37-39), but the appeal was abandoned: Attorney General's Office, 4 December 1856, PDF p51 (PAGE 43): 'In the case of the claim of Petronillo Rios, confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, case no. two hundred and forty one (241), appeal will not be prosecuted by the United States' (filed 21 Feb 1857, PDF p52, PAGE 44). Confirmation therefore stood.

corrections.grantee: Pedro Narvaez per the concession decree, PDF p21 (351 SD PAGE 16): 'declaro dueno en propiedad a D.n Pedro Narvaez del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles'. Petronilo Rios acquired it from Narvaez, first by an act of assignment endorsed on the grant 5 April 1845 and then by a formal deed of sale before the 1st Alcalde of Monterey, 30 March 1846 (petition PDF p9, PAGE 4; deed PDF p23, PAGE 28, signed Manuel Diaz, alcalde, and Pedro Narvaez).

notes: Dominant error class: the register carries the claimant (Petronilo Rios, the name on the red label) as grantee. Hoffman 1862 ('Pedro Narvaez') agrees with the case file against the register. Year and governor in the register are correct. Two things a re-reader should know. (1) The file explains WHY Narvaez never lived there: Jose Rafael Gonzalez testified (PDF p12-13, PAGES 6-7) that 'in consequence of the official position of Narvaez he was unable to reside on the Ranch himself. He sent a Mayor Domo there with servants, and cattle and horses ... but in consequence of the depredations committed by Indians he became disgusted and sold the Ranch to Petronillo Rios'; Narvaez had left for Tepic, Mexico, by 1846-47. (2) The expediente records a boundary dispute settled in person before Micheltorena at Monterey on 16 May 1844 between Capt. Pedro Narvaez and Sr. Arce, 'quedando la parte del Paso de Robles para el Sor. Narvaez y el Sor. Arce el de Santa Ysabel' (PDF p21, PAGE 16). A stray leaf, PDF p47 (PAGE 35), is a notice of appeal by Petronilo Rios in a DIFFERENT claim, Land Commission No. 622, 'for the mission lands of the Ex mission of San Miguel' - filed 23 Oct 1855 and bound into this docket; do not read it as part of the Paso de Robles appeal. Patent not in the file; Phase C should check GLO for the claimed 20 July 1866 patent no. 320. Note the register spells the claimant 'Petrenelo Rios'; the file writes 'Petronillo Rios' (label 'PETRONILLA RIOS').

name.evidence: Grant title, PDF p20 (97 ND PAGE 16): 'el terreno conocido con el nombre de Pastoria de las Borregas'; English translation PDF p24 (PAGE 20): 'the tract of land known by the name of Pastoria de las Borregas'. Board decree PDF p42 (PAGE 37): 'a part of the place known by the name of Pastoria de las Borregas'. Note the docket also carries the alias 'Refugio': the transcript title page (PDF p4, PAGE 1) and the Secretary's certificate (PDF p43, PAGE 38) both style it 'Refugio', and the claimant's petition (PDF p9, PAGE 4) calls it 'the Rancho del Refugio or Pastoria de las Borregas'. There is no red case label in this scan; PDF p1 is the microfilm slip, 'LAND CASE 97 ND / 505 pages.'

year.evidence: Spanish title, PDF p21 (97 ND PAGE 17): 'Dado en Monterey a quince de Enero de mil ochocientos cuarenta y dos. Juan B. Alvarado. Manuel Jimeno, Srio.' Sworn English translation, PDF p25 (PAGE 21): 'Given at Monterey the fifteenth of January 1842.' The expediente decree agrees, PDF p30 (PAGE 26): 'Monterey Enero 15 de 1842 ... declaro a D.n Franc.o Estrada dueno en propiedad del terreno nombrado Pastoria de los Borregos'; registry entries at the Prefecture of the 1st District are dated 'Monterey, 16 de Enero de 1842' (PDF p21).

governor.evidence: PDF p20 (PAGE 16), head of the title: 'Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador constitucional del Departamento de las Californias'; signed 'Juan B. Alvarado. Manuel Jimeno, Srio.' PDF p21 (PAGE 17). Expediente decree closes (PDF p32, PAGE 27 / translation PDF p37, PAGE 32): 'Sor. Don Juan B. Alvarado Constitutional Governor of the Department of the Californias thus Commanded decreed and Signed.' Alvarado's own marginal order of 23 Feb 1841 is at PDF p35 (PAGE 30).

grantee.evidence: The grant itself, PDF p20 (97 ND PAGE 16): 'Por cuanto D. Francisco Estrada, ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia, el terreno conocido con el nombre de Pastoria de las Borregas ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado, declarando le la propiedad de el por las presentes letras.' Sworn translation PDF p24 (PAGE 20): 'Whereas D.n Francisco Estrada has sought to obtain for his personal benefit & that of his family the tract of land known by the name of Pastoria de las Borregas ... I have conceded to him the said tract of land, declaring to him the ownership thereof by these present letters.' Mariano Castro is the U.S.-era claimant only. The Board's own opinion, PDF p39 (PAGE 34), states it plainly: 'on the 2d day of January A.D. 1842, one Don Francisco Estrada obtained from Governor Alvarado a grant for the place called Pastoria de los Borregas, that some time in the year 1845 the said grantee died, without wife or children ... that the father of said grantee, as heir of his son Francisco ... conveyed all his interest in & to said tract of land to the petitioner in this case.'

land_case.evidence: Every leaf stamped '97 ND'; PDF p1 microfilm slip 'LAND CASE 97 ND'; District Court wrapper PDF p44 'U.S. DISTRICT COURT, [Northern] District of California ... Transcript of the Record from the Board of U.S. Land Commissioners, In Case No. 257, Filed Sept. 13, 1854' with '97 ND' stamped over it; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_nd097.pdf. (Board docket No. 257, per the title page PDF p4 and the certificate PDF p43, matching Hoffman's commission_no 257.)

outcome.evidence: Board Decree of Confirmation, PDF p41-42 (97 ND PAGES 36-37): 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the said petitioner is valid, & it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed. The lands of which confirmation are hereby made are a part of the place known by the name of Pastoria de las Borregas ... containing in all two square leagues, a little more or less, excepting from this confirmation two tracts of land embraced within the foregoing boundaries' (Alpheus Felch, Thompson Campbell, R. Aug. Thompson, Commissioners), filed 24 January 1854. The US appealed: Attorney General Cushing, 30 November 1854, PDF p45 (PAGE 39), 'the appeal in the district court of the United States for the Northern district of California will be prosecuted by the United States'. The District Court confirmed as well: the judge's bench notes on the later survey hearing, PDF p511 (PAGE 501), record 'The decree limits the quantity to 2 leagues ... The Court not satisfied with this proof confined the grantee to 2 leagues. The case comes up now on objections to the survey.' A co-claimant's separate outcome is noted at PDF p505 (PAGE 495): 'Murphy, who has a separate final confirmation for 4894 35/100 acres.'

corrections.grantee: Francisco Estrada per the grant, PDF p20/p24 (97 ND PAGES 16 and 20). Mariano Castro took by conveyance from Jose Maria Estrada, Francisco's father and heir: the cession endorsed on the back of the title reads 'Como heredero del finado Francisco Estrada, digo que cedo voluntariamente a favor del ciud.no Mariano Castro, los dos sitios que se espresan en este titulo. Buenavista, 17 de Marzo 1845. Jose Maria Estrada' (PDF p21, PAGE 17; English at PDF p26, PAGE 22), judicially authenticated before Regidor Ignacio Esquer at San Jose on 27 January 1846 (PDF p27 and p29, PAGES 18-19).

notes: Dominant error class: the register carries the U.S. claimant (Mariano Castro) as grantee. Hoffman 1862 ('Francisco Estrada') agrees with the case file against the register. Year and governor in the register are correct. Three cautions for a re-reader. (1) The BOARD'S OPINION MISDATES TWO KEY DOCUMENTS and should not be used as the source for either: PDF p39 (PAGE 34) says the grant issued 'on the 2d day of January A.D. 1842' where the title itself twice says 15 January 1842, and says Jose Maria Estrada conveyed 'on the 17th day of March A.D. 1849' where the endorsement on the title is dated 17 March 1845. Grade against the title (PDF p20-21, p24-25), not the opinion. (2) The confirmation carried two express exceptions, which is why the eventual patent is only 4,172 acres against a two-league grant: the land of the Santa Clara Indian YNIGO, reserved to him by the Departmental Assembly and noted by Micheltorena on the back of the original grant, 'Monterey, February 14th 1844. (Signed) Manuel Micheltorena' (PDF p21 and p40, PAGES 17 and 35-36); and the tracts Castro had already deeded to Martin Murphy, filed in case No. 90 (PDF p40, PAGE 36). (3) This is a 517-image, 363MB file; roughly 460 of its pages are a long survey contest among Castro, Murphy, R. Walkinshaw (claiming under the Ynigo grant), and intervenors Jones, Sullivan and Wallace (PDF p505-517, PAGES 495-505), which is where the acreage was finally fixed. The Estrada expediente itself is a traced copy borrowed from case No. 90 by stipulation of 21 Sept 1853 (PDF p18-19, PAGES 14-15) and certified by Surveyor General Samuel D. King, 26 Feb 1852 (PDF p33, PAGE 28). Original judicial measurement of 1842 was lost: Sunol testified the leaves recording it 'had been cut out' of the San Jose prefecture book (PDF p18, PAGE 14). No patent copy in the file; Phase C should check GLO for the claimed 17 Sept 1881 patent no. 144.
